extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent office staff involved in PCT international applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and formal rules under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) governing amendments, communications, publication, translations, restoration of rights, and related national processing steps for international patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for amendments under Article 19
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit referred to in Article 19 is two months from the date of transmittal of the international search report to the International Bureau and to the applicant by the International Searching Authority or 16 months from the priority date, whichever expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment made under Article 19 received by the International Bureau after expiration of the applicable time limit shall be considered received on the last day of that time limit if it reaches the Bureau before international publication and the technical preparations for international publication have been completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file Article 19 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments made under Article 19 shall be filed directly with the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of Article 19 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application has been filed in a language other than the language in which it is published, any amendment under Article 19 shall be in the language of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under Article 19(1) — form and content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement referred to in Article 19(1) must be in the language of publication and shall not exceed 500 words if in English or translated into English; it shall be identified by a heading (e.g., “Statement under Article 19(1)”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement shall contain no disparaging comments on the international search report or the relevance of citations in that report. Reference to citations in the ISR may be made only in connection with an amendment to the relevant claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of amendments — replacement claims sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: When making amendments under Article 19 the applicant must submit replacement sheet(s) containing a complete set of claims in replacement of all claims originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The replacement sheet(s) must be accompanied by a letter which: (i) identifies the claims that differ from the originally filed claims and draws attention to the differences; (ii) identifies claims originally filed which are cancelled; and (iii) indicates the basis for the amendments in the application as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication to designated Offices not prior to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The communication provided for in Article 20 shall be effected by the International Bureau to each designated Office in accordance with Rule 93 bis.1 but, subject to Rule 47.4, not prior to the international publication of the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau notification of receipt to designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall notify each designated Office of the fact and date of receipt of the record copy and of the fact and date of receipt of any priority document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification is to be effected in accordance with Rule 93 bis.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of late amendments to designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment received by the International Bureau within the time limit under Rule 46.1 which was not included in the communication under Article 20 shall be communicated promptly to the designated Offices by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The International Bureau shall notify the applicant accordingly when such amendments are communicated to designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to applicant after 28 months regarding designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Promptly after expiration of 28 months from the priority date, the International Bureau shall send a notice to the applicant indicating which designated Offices have requested that communication under Article 20 be effected and which have not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: That notice is accepted by designated Offices as conclusive evidence either that the communication was effected on the date specified (for those who requested it) or that the Contracting State does not require furnishing by the applicant of a copy of the international application (for those who did not request it).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required for communication prepared by International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The copies required for communication under Article 20 shall be prepared by the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further details concerning the copies required may be provided in the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express requests under Article 23(2) prior to international publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant makes an express request to a designated Office under Article 23(2) prior to international publication, the International Bureau shall, upon request of the applicant or the designated Office, promptly effect the communication provided for in Article 20 to that Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and means of international publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The form in which and the means by which international applications are published shall be governed by the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the international publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication shall contain a standardized front page, the description, the claims, the drawings (if any), subject to paragraph (g) the international search report or the declaration under Article 17(2)(a), any statement filed under Article 19(1) (unless non-compliant), and various additional items such as indications relating to deposited biological material, priority claim information, certain declarations and corrections, and information concerning restoration of priority requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific subitems listed include: standardized front page; description; claims; drawings; ISR or Article17 declaration; Article19(1) statement (unless not compliant); requests/rectifications received before technical preparations; indications on deposited biological material and date received; information concerning priority claims and certain declarations/corrections received before prescribed time limits; and info on requests under Rule 26 bis.3 for restoration of priority and receiving Office decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page required data and indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, the front page shall include data taken from the request sheet and other prescribed data, a figure or figures if drawings exist, the abstract (English first if bilingual), and where applicable, indications of declarations, special filing-date situations, presence of information under Rule 26 bis.2(d), restoration requests, or removal of erroneously filed elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a declaration under Article 17(2)(a) has issued, the front page must conspicuously refer to that fact and need not include drawing or abstract. Figures on the front page selected per Rule 8.2 and may be reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of abstracts, translations, amended claims, and ISR on publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is not enough room on the front page for the abstract or its translation, the abstract (and translation when required) shall appear on the back of the front page. If claims have been amended under Article 19, publication shall contain the full text of the claims both as filed and as amended, and any Article 19(1) statement unless non-compliant; date of receipt of amended claims by the IB shall be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ISR is not available at the time of completion of technical preparations, the front page shall indicate that and state that the ISR will be separately published with a revised front page when available. If time limit for Article19 amendments has not expired at completion, front page shall so state and indicate that amended claims and Article19(1) statement (if filed and compliant) will be published promptly with a revised front page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission from publication upon reasoned request
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau may omit from publication any information at the applicant's reasoned request received prior to completion of technical preparations if it finds that: (i) the information does not obviously serve the purpose of informing the public about the application; (ii) publication would clearly prejudice personal or economic interests of any person; and (iii) there is no prevailing public interest to have access to that information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 26.4 applies mutatis mutandis as to how the applicant should present the information; receiving Office, ISA, IPER or IB may suggest omission where criteria are met; if IB omits information also present in file copies elsewhere, it shall promptly notify those Offices/Authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application is filed in one of the listed 'languages of publication' (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish), it shall be published in the language in which it was filed. If not filed in a language of publication but a translation into a language of publication has been furnished, it shall be published in the language of that translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If published in a language other than English, the international search report (to the extent published), any Article17 declaration, the title, the abstract and any text matter pertaining to the figures accompanying the abstract shall be published both in that language and in English; translations not furnished by applicant shall be prepared under IB responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earlier publication on applicant's request and special fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant asks for earlier publication under Articles 21(2)(b) and 64(3)(c)(i) and the ISR or Article17 declaration is not yet available, the International Bureau shall collect a special publication fee (amount set in Administrative Instructions) and shall effect publication promptly after the applicant asked for it and, if fee due, after receipt of the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication notices of late notifications or withdrawals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notification under Rule29.1(ii) reaches the IB too late to prevent international publication, the IB shall promptly publish a notice in the Gazette reproducing the essence of such notification. If the international application, designation, or priority claim is withdrawn after technical preparations are completed, notice of withdrawal shall be published in the Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification by Contracting States of translation and national fee requirements (Article 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State requiring the furnishing of a translation or the payment of a national fee (or both) under Article 22 shall notify the International Bureau of the languages from which and into which it requires translation and of the amount of the national fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Contracting State not requiring furnishing of a copy under Article 22 shall notify the IB accordingly. Such notifications shall be promptly published in the Gazette. Changes in requirements must be notified and published; changes that impose new translation languages take effect only for applications filed later than two months after Gazette publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language(s) into which translation may be required by designated Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The language into which a translation may be required must be an official language of the designated Office. If several official languages exist, no translation may be required if the international application is in one of them; where several exist and a translation must be furnished, the applicant may choose any of those languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding the above, if national law prescribes use of one language for foreigners, a translation into that language may be required. Information on designated Offices' practices under this provision shall be published by the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements under Article 19 and Rule 13 bis.4 considered part of application for Article 22 purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of Article 22 and Rule 49, any statement made under Article 19(1) and any indication furnished under Rule 13 bis.4 shall, subject to Rule 49.5(c) and (h), be considered part of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant did not furnish a translation of a statement made under Article 19(1), the designated Office may disregard that statement (Rule 49.5(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of national form not required
rubrics_metrics.description: No applicant shall be required to use a national form when performing the acts referred to in Article 22.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and physical requirements for translations under Article 22
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation must contain the description (subject to certain exceptions), the claims, any text matter of the drawings and the abstract. If required by the designated Office, the translation shall also contain the request, both claims as filed and as amended (if Article19 amendments exist), and be accompanied by a copy of the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: designated Offices may accept sequence-listing parts under Rule12.1(d) without translation of language-dependent free text; drawing text translations may be provided by pasting translations onto copies or by new drawings; the expression "Fig." need not be translated; where copies/drawings do not comply with physical requirements, DO may invite correction within a reasonable time; if translation of an Article19 statement or abstract not furnished, DO may disregard or invite translation within reasonable time. DOs cannot require translation to comply with physical requirements beyond those for the international application as filed. If ISA established a title under Rule37.2, the translation shall contain that title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disregard or invitation to supply missing translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a designated Office requires translations of both the claims as filed and as amended and the applicant furnishes only one of the two required translations, the designated Office may disregard the claims lacking translation or invite the applicant to furnish the missing translation within a reasonable time; failure to furnish may lead to disregard of those claims or consideration of the application withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of rights after failure to perform Article 22 acts
rubrics_metrics.description: If the effect under Article 11(3) ceased because the applicant failed to perform acts under Article 22 within the time limit, the designated Office shall, on the applicant's request and subject to conditions, reinstate rights if it finds the delay was unintentional or (at DO's option) occurred despite due care being taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be submitted and the acts performed within either two months from removal of the cause or 12 months from expiration of the applicable time limit (whichever expires first), unless national law permits later submission. The request must state reasons for failure; national law may require fees or declarations/evidence; DO shall not refuse without giving applicant opportunity to make observations within a reasonable time. Transitional compatibility provisions may apply for certain dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indications as to protection sought for national processing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant wishes the international application to be treated in a designated State as an application for a different kind of protection (e.g., not for a patent but another protection under Article 43/44), the applicant shall indicate this to the designated Office when performing the acts under Article 22; if treated as an addition, continuation, etc., indicate the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no express indication is made but the national fee paid corresponds to a particular kind of protection, payment shall be considered an indication of the applicant's wish and the DO shall inform the applicant accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for furnishing indications as to protection sought
rubrics_metrics.description: No designated Office shall require that the applicant furnish the indications referred to in Rule 49 bis.1 before performing the acts under Article 22. The applicant may, if national law permits, furnish such indications or convert to another kind of protection at any later time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of restoration of priority by the receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the receiving Office has restored a right of priority under Rule 26 bis.3 based on due care, that restoration shall, subject to exceptions, be effective in each designated State; where restoration was based on unintentionality, effectiveness depends on designated State national law providing for that criterion (or a more favorable one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A receiving Office decision shall not be effective in a designated State where that State finds that a requirement under Rule 26 bis.3 was not complied with. A designated Office shall not review the receiving Office decision unless it reasonably doubts compliance and must notify the applicant and allow observations. A designated State is not bound by a receiving Office's refusal to restore; where receiving Office refused, a DO may treat that as a request for restoration to the DO within the DO's time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of right of priority by designated Office — criteria and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A designated Office shall restore the right of priority upon request if it finds the failure to file within the priority period either occurred despite due care required by the circumstances or was unintentional (each DO must apply at least one of those criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests shall be filed within one month from the applicable Article 22 time limit (or within one month from date of receipt if express request under Art23(2)); must state reasons and preferably be accompanied by declarations/evidence and any fee. The DO may require declarations/evidence within a reasonable time; may charge a fee; shall not refuse without giving the applicant opportunity to comment. DOs that have national law with more favorable requirements may apply that law instead. Each DO shall inform the IB of which criteria it applies, and that information will be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty under Article 22(3) — national time limit notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State allowing a time limit later than those in Article 22(1) or (2) shall notify the International Bureau of the time limits so fixed; such notifications shall be published in the Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications shortening previously fixed time limits become effective for international applications filed after three months from Gazette publication; lengthening notifications become effective on Gazette publication (or later date if fixed by State) for pending and later-filed applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for presenting request to send copies (Article 25(1)(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit referred to in Article 25(1)(c) for presenting the request to send copies shall be two months computed from the date of the notification sent to the applicant under Rule 20.4(i), 24.2(c) or 29.1(ii).
